就目前来看落差挺大的，武器只有4把，每把升级满之后有4种形态（改变攻击形态的就一种，大多就是更改了一丁点数值），npc有六七个，但是能给你局外成长的就只有最开始遇到的两个（武器升级，人物属性提升），其他遇到的都只是过剧情然后给你货币，同质化过于严重，每次我遇到一个新的npc，我都以为会给我个新系统什么的，谁知道就是几十金币（用来升级属性和武器）？？？ 看似挺多的遗物，给的数值过于保守，导致基本上很难爽起来，就算胡了也难，并且有些遗物效果也过于令人难绷，比如完成一波遭遇战，最大生命值+1，这种就是让你前期更舒服一点，然后到了后期一点用没有，硬占地方，我就给换了，然后发现，我攒了很久的最大生命值也掉了，本来就是高风险低收货，还因为后期没用换了之后收货也给我撤回了，我就？？？ 还有那个遗物的格子系统，刚开始以为那个格子最起码在后续剧情里是慢慢可以扩充的，最后会到一整个正方形，但是玩到通关了，所有npc遇一遍了，都没看到可以扩充格子的地方，所以可用的格子就那么多，弄个正方形给菱形围起来干嘛，纯纯为了好看吗？？ 遗物格子问题，只有同一颜色遗物三连之后才会给相应武器伤害，卡牌伤害之类的有加成，没有三连之前只会有遗物的基础能力，然而角色属性过低，尽管是成倍增长的武器伤害，因需三连才可提升，导致想要的流派到最后也就300%左右的伤害（并且绝大多数伤害提升感觉都是加法运算），而敌人生命值基本上是指数级增长，到后期基本上很难砍得动，都是刮痧。 骰子系统，我一直想着最起码骰子可以让我慢慢多起来，谁知道玩到最后还是只有一颗，每次扔出去还得捡，就算点了可以自动回收的天赋，也需要3s钟才可以回收，离得远回收到手里还得1s，相当于4s扔一个骰子，这时候用武器不知道打多少伤害了，骰子流派就纯纯坐牢。 卡牌系统，每次遇到新卡牌，总觉得旧卡牌可以回收，不说卡牌升级了，连回收成每局的局内货币都不行，我真是有一点点难绷，反正每遇到一个npc都基本上很少给到我正反馈，每次看到给我货币之后就没下文了，就让我头疼。 反正暂时玩的正式版还是感觉爽感不足，游戏体验一般般，真要买的话等打折吧 对了，还有，游戏中偶尔会遇到精英怪，但是你知道打完精英怪，打我好长血给我什么吗，局外升级用的货币二选一，遇到几次之后真的心态直接没了

[table][th] Review by [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34633003-Gaming-Masterpieces/lists/] Gaming Masterpieces [/url] - The greatest games of all time on Steam. [/th][/table] Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, although not one of those world-shattering Tier 1 masterpieces. Just a nice little game that is fun to explore. After Hades, a million games copied its mechanics. I am not saying that all of them were bad, just not very innovative. And, after playing Hades for a few hours, my appetite for the genre was also a bit saturated. I did play some of the copycats, though. This is one of them. It feels like Hades on steroids. You run around like on Speed. Like in the great movie Run Lola Run (1998). Defeat enemies, race to the next room, defeat enemies. Attack, dash, throw your (exploding) dice. The living dice is really a fun addition - throw it, hope for a good number, and then pick it up again. Until you die and wake up in the Sanctuary (hub), which you slowly expand by bringing more and more of the creatures you meet there. Your character gets stronger, and every few runs you get closer to your goal of defeating Mare. Knowing the original Lost in Random (a decent 3D action-adventure) game helps understanding the strange universe the game takes place, but is not necessary. You meet a few old friends (or foes), like the ugly toad Aama who now sells you blessings. Or the evil Mare, of course. The game plays quite - polished. Fast-paced combat, beautiful visuals (in Lost in Random style), voice-overs, quite a lot of random stuff you find to experiment with, and permanent upgrades you unlock after grinding. [u][b] Conclusion:[/b][/u] Hadeslike. If this genre exists. Or just a good, little fast-paced action roguelike (similar to Hades).

Short fun little game, mechanics similar to Hades (but no dash strike), super charming, story is meh/ok. Wait for a promo maybe before buying

If Tim Burton ever decided to craft an action roguelike, it would probably resemble Lost in Random: The Eternal Die. It excels in every single facet of the genre, creating a truly unforgettable gaming universe you won't want to leave. Fortune favors those who dive in.

[h1]rouge、骰子以及三消[/h1] 评分：7.4/10 《迷失混沌王国：永恒之骰》是一款暗黑童话题材的动作类Roguelike游戏。剧情说是衔接了前作，不过我没玩过前作。不太要紧，本作的剧情非常简单，甚至可以说是薄弱。前作的角色亚历山德拉女王被邪恶骰魔击败并囚禁。然后女王和骰子伙伴一同越狱，在过程中拯救一些也是被关押的NPC，最终完成对骰魔的复仇。 本作的主要玩法就是动作rouge。和大部分rouge游戏一样，角色有分为局外成长和局内成长，金币也同样局内局外的。游戏中主角可以积攒红币、蓝币两种物品用于局外成长，分别可以解锁更多的武器和激活更多的被动、特质。游戏的武器总共有宝剑、弓箭、长枪、大锤四把，但每把武器还可以进行四种方向的强化，同类武器不同强化方向的武器有时区别很大，所以能说是有十六种武器。游戏的各个武器手感都很好且各有特点，宝剑的均衡，弓箭的远攻，长枪的快攻速，大锤伤害高。每种武器都可以蓄力，并且因为强化方向的不同，蓄力攻击的形式都会改变，这个还蛮值得体验一遍的。可惜每一次越狱只让使用一中武器，中途不让更换。游戏的另一局外成长可以归纳为被动或特质，比如加伤害、复活、减少局内商店物品的价格，每个特质有左右两个效果可以选择，不能同时携带。局内的成长放下面讲。局内还有个金币系统，用于每关购买物品（加最大生命值、回血、宝箱等），不过金币其实蛮难的，要么过房间有概率可以出现，要么房间内有些瓶瓶罐罐可以敲碎，然而掉率感人。除攻击外，游戏有个卡牌系统，其实就是技能，每次开局会随机刷一个，后面遇到也能换，技能的效果各种各样，有的好用有的鸡肋，释放技能所需的能量来自于攻击敌人。技能种类不够丰富就是了，大部分的效果趋于同质，就是远远的扔个什么东西出去攻击。然后角色闪避的无敌帧很宽容，也只有一秒左右的冷却时间。 游戏的特色之一，扔骰子。战斗时角色除了攻击和释放技能外，还可以扔骰子攻击，可以自己瞄准，手柄也有一点辅助瞄准。扔骰子本身带有一点伤害，但游戏的特点在于，随着流程的推进角色能开很多宝箱遗物（可以理解为rouge种类里的BUFF），这些遗物有相当一部分和扔骰子挂钩，比如说扔出三点五点点，会释放闪电或者飞镖之类的；扔出奇数偶数又有些其他什么的效果；扔出骰子再捡起会生成一个毒物区等等等等，效果可以叠加，还挺好玩的。 游戏的另一特色，三消。三消跟刚刚提到遗物（BUFF）有关，游戏中的遗物除本身效果外，会附带有颜色（红黄蓝绿紫），有的还是多种颜色覆盖，然后有个遗物格子供玩家放置，当三种以上同一颜色的遗物放置在一条直线时（横的、竖的、斜的都可以），就可以进行三消，三消后会触发角色局内数值的提升（红色加50%攻击伤害、黄的加技能50%攻击伤害、还有加骰子伤害、加暴击几率的等五种数值）。因为三消的机制，玩家在选择和放置遗物时需要一定的思考和策略，遗物可以进行替换，但替换后原遗物效果就没了。房间奖励和商店会有染色剂，可以进行染色更方便的触发三消。 游戏总共有四张地图，地图场景的画风会有所区别，冰的、火的、丛林的等，不过美术都有很明显的童话味。每个地图由若干个小房间相互串联，清完一个房间的所有怪物就可以通向下一个房间，除去战斗房间外，每个地图会有一个商店、小游戏、闯关的房间。有的房间会有一些地形、沼泽、机关的设计。每个地图都会有一个守关boss，击败boss直接会进入下一个地图，最后一个boss就是骰魔。除去战斗的时候，都可以随时的存档保存。 一些缺点： 1.关卡和内容相比起价格来说还是偏少 2.遗物格子太小了，玩到后面根本不考虑遗物效果了，无脑触发三消堆数值 3.重复游玩价值并不高，通关一遍后，就是boss数值和攻击方式有所增加 4.卡牌技能着实很多都太鸡肋，种类也少 5.蛮关键的一点，rouge游戏没有重随功能，卡牌鸡肋不能重随，遗物宝箱不能重随，染色剂全用不上也不能重随。

These "Hades" type dungeon crawlers may be a dime a dozen lately, but this one is well worth it. Game play is fluid, story and characters are charming, and the game length doesn't overstay its welcome. High recommended

I was super excited for this game to release since the first "Lost in Random" was so good. It had a great art style and theme that reminds me of Alice in Wonderland. MY biggest issue with this game is the fact that its a rouge-like. There is honestly nothing wrong with rouge-likes but the first game was an amazing story driven action adventure with an amazing mechanic with the dice. The story was interesting and combat was unique with its dice rolling mechanic. The Eternal Die doesn't have the same pull with its story or characters. The outfits were cool but would have been better it they gave bonus stats or additional perks. Combat was good and felt smooth but the dice roll mechanic was very basic. Sure you can make builds based around rolling the dice or card abilities but they are very limited. On top of repetitive combat the game was much shorter than I was expecting. As of right now I cannot recommend it and only hope additional content is added because I think it can still be good. In its current state its just limited.

This is wonderfull little game! If Hades II is overwhelming and a bit too dynamic at times - this is a spin you may like on the genre. And if you, like me, already like the first Lost in Random game, you need to play this! Of course there are some things I would rebalance and fixed for even more fun. But this is a very good and capable little game. Played it on steam deck and it was a blast! 10/10 hooked me way more than it should have

This is a really sad negative review I'm writing here, because you can tell all the effort and hardwork the devs put into this game, but no matter how much I tried, I could just never enjoy playing it, so I felt like I had to write this review. Lost In Random: The Eternal Die is what you could call a top-down hack & slash action roguelike HEAVILY inspired by Hades in almost every sense. The camera angle, the feeling of combat, the upgrade system, the different weapons with their own different forms, the story-telling and so on... So, let's start talking about the good aspects of the game, which are a lot: -Graphics and animations are gorgeous. Every single visual aspect in this game is 10/10 and, what's even better, performance is surprisingly outstanding, something you don't see that often nowadays. -Voice acting, as expected, is also top-tier, reminding me a lot to Hades. -Controls are really responsive and combining/chaining attacks feels really smooth. -There is plenty of replayability in terms of weapons. Like I mentioned, there are 4 or 5 different starting weapons, each one with 4 different varieties. There are also different upgrades and, more importantly, different active skills you can equip during every run to try. The game also counts with 5 extra difficulties that will get modified during every run (you basically choose mutators during the run, so the difficulty won't be the same every time). So, the previous aspects of the game sound like a good deal, right? Then why the bad review? 3 main reasons: -First, the one I disliked the most, even when I said the camera is like in Hades, it is like 1.5 times closer, which wouldn't be that much of a pain if it wasn't because almost every enemy in the game attacks with a huge range (shooting/throwing projectiles or attacking with really long melee weapons), so a lot of times you will get attack from outside your visual range without even seeing something attempting to attack you. Because of the same, you might dash to the bottom right or left to avoid an attack because it looks clear enough, but the moment the dash is over you realize you are on top of a trap or a projectile that couldn't see because of the camera. And I'm not talking about isolated moments where this happens, it will be like that most of the run, reason why the most effective way to play the game is staying as far as possible from everything. Just take a look to a screenshot from this game and compare it with one from Hades and you will see the difference. -Second, staggering is inconsistent. You not always stagger enemies, just some attacks do (most of the time, the last attack of a combo), so, if that one attack doesn't hit an enemy that you were hitting in the middle of the fight, you are doomed to get damage for trying to have fun by fighting. And there are a lot of enemies per area, so this is another reason why the best way to play this game is just staying as far as possible, ideally with a range weapon. -Third, and probably the strongest weak point of the game in general is that it is almost impossible to feel strong during a run. Yes, there are a lot of different upgrades with a pretty unique system where you can match upgrades of the same color for extra buffs, and yes, there are a lot of synergies that are honestly pretty cool to see in action. However, once you are full of upgrades, and it could be something like "you hit them with poison, poison chains lightning, lightning bounce over more enemies and then they burn, if they burn they explode and blah blah blah", which sounds really good, but by the end all of that will be just a little bit of damage... as every upgrade feels in this game. The best way to scale your own damage if by matching as many of the same color as you can, and even so you will be dealing less than 5% of damage to even the weakest of enemies by the end of the run. The only upgrade that feels really strong is the one that you get extra damage per enemy defeated, but you have to play it perfectly, because you will lose the buff the moment you get damage. Also, meta-progression is incredibly slow (really expensive and just for a little bit of damage or resistance). I beated the game around 3 times (in different difficulties), and still got like 25 extra max HP, 20% extra damage, 1 HP healed after every room, 15% discount on my first purchase, something like 2% extra dodge chance and stuff like that. If you, again, compare with Hades, you will notice the huge differences. As if this wasn't enough, the difficulties scale way too fast and, don't get me wrong, I'm not saying it is too hard or impossible to beat, it is just becomes way too tedious because they get stronger and stronger, tougher and tougher while you barely get any reward that makes a difference. Basically that, if you already didn't like Hades, this game is definitely not for you, because the only boss variety you will find is the first boss because you fight 2 bosses at the same time and there are 3 different options there. If the visuals and story telling are enough for you to get hooked with a game, then this is definitely for you. For me this is something like a 6/10 (mostly because I think every aspect, but the gameplay itself are top quality) and you can check out some gameplay here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PV5Yfk0-8iY (I honestly think this game would have been better as a linear hack & slash).

[h1]Lost in unbalance[/h1] So here we are another Lost in Random game. I loved the first one. It wasn't without flaws but it was enjoyable and quite unique. And the sequel and and absolute opposite of everything the first one was. Except that it isn't bad although not great either. So first things first. Story. Well not much of it here. Yes there's some sort of story and same lore which is a good thing because in my opinion developers built and excellent lore with the first game and can easily expand it into several games and spin-offs. It just feel unfair that this one is called Lost in Random. It's confusing for the old players since the games are entirely different. While the first one was pretty casual – this one could be hardcore. This time it's a rogue-like and very similar to Hades, often too similar. I don't even know what to say regarding gameplay...well it's like Hades, literally. You have four biomes and four bosses although in one biome two bosses count as one so lets make it five. You start by picking you weapon (sword, mace, bow or spear) and go on clearing room after room. After defeating enemies in each room you get a chest with a random reward. You become stronger by putting coloured relics into empty slots. If you match the colours of at least three relics you get a boost in one of four stats – weapons damage, conjurations (like magic), card damage and Fortune (your little die friend). Each relic also has its individual effects, it could be anything really, from increased damage to passive damage, various negative effect and so on. You get the idea. If you put a new relic on top of another the old one and its effect disappear. So you have your weapon, Fortune (a die) and a card. You pick the card in the first room and later depending on rng you can change to some other one. Cards are like spell attacks, they consume energy and deal magic damage like poison, stun, freeze, fire and so on. Fortune on the other hand can do passive damage and also deals small amount of damage when you throw it onto the enemies. That's pretty much regarding attacks. The game is simple yet could be challenging to master. You must attack quickly, dodge in time and manage your relics wisely. So you clear the rooms, get rewards, find special rooms which give you rewards based on rng (you throw fortune and depending where it lands you get a reward). There's a also a shop in each biome. And then you fight the main boss of each area. After you die you restart your run. But with collected materials you can upgrade your weapons (each weapons has three trees) and with collected pip dust you buy and upgrade blessings – these are permanent buffs like more hp, higher damage, more money and so on. Now why such title you wonder? The game is unbalanced. It's made for ranged build only or for passive damage builds. Since enemies are extremely aggressive, fast and there are a lot of them you must dodge, dodge a lot. But you can do only once every one second or so. There's double or triple dodge like in Hades. Why this is a problem? Because if four enemies jump you in quick succession you can't dodge them. Another thing is that enemies while jumping on you, track you so even you get out of the way they bend their trajectory to hit you. And this why ranged weapons work and melee weapons suck. Since you keep your distance with a bow and you can stay out of range and only dodge once every 3+ seconds. Melee just doesn't work. Last boss with melee build is insane, especially keeping in mind there are achievements of beating every boss without taking damage. This is poor design. Game should be equally enjoyable and beatable with any weapon. That's where Hades succeeded and this one failed completely. Oh by the way for those who can't play difficult games there's an easy mode. It helps so don't be afraid to try it out. Thanks for adding that. There's also lack of motivation to play it after you beat the last boss. Hades had fun challenge modes, lots and lots of story. But here? Nothing. Challenge mode isn't fun, it's frustrating because you get debuffs but still have single dodge and constantly dodge into AOE areas or enemies. Graphically the game is great. Everything looks awesome and visual design in general is great. Maybe bosses lack character. Sound direction is ok. Music is forgettable but voice acting is really good. Performance is absolutely flawless. It's rare to see a game these days even if it has simple graphics which runs on a potatoe. My GPU died one day and I was without it for few days. I played this on cpu only, using iGPU integrated into cpu at 3440x1440 while streaming on twitch through OBS. Framerates were smooth and in between 60-90fps. I was shocked. Great job developers. So is it worth getting? If you expect the old good Lost in Random then no. If you want a decent rogue-like because you're waiting for Hades 2 full release and want to satisfy that thirst – yes get it. You'll have some fun. 全资源为美术服务的极端作品， 制作组并不在意自己的游戏是否好玩， 开发重心以及制作精力全花在不用放大镜根本看不清的皮肤身上， 咱也不喷制作组不尊重玩家或者傲慢啥的 人家只是沉迷在艺术创作不能自拔 游戏定位 和捆绑包另一位重量级reignbreaker一样，这同样不是正经肉鸽 他的制作标准完全是arpg，只不过穿插了些无足轻重的随机要素 正确玩法是走走停停，欣赏沿路的哥特是风景， 打怪什么的都是附赠的 战斗体验 客观来讲这游戏是下限高上限低 假如以简单模式开局，每次死亡都会获得5%的减伤buff，上限是65% 以此加持下，你能很直观的感觉到虽然可能每局都在死，但每局走到的地方会更远 隐约中给你一种似乎你在变强的错觉 换句话说这游戏不存在不通关的可能性，保底你能体验到制作组的匠心剧情 最大的缺陷在于数值，这游戏完全不存在任何爽度 作为特色的连连看/卡牌/骰子bd构筑的终点是堆数值，整体攻击模式以及艺术呈现不会发生质变 我最数值的一集是晕锤，平a暴击400+，蓄力暴击1000+，数值是初始的50倍 然后呢？打4层小怪依然要a两下，打boss体验依旧只是花的时间变少了些许 大体上这个游戏的战斗风格就是魂游式的抱头鼠窜再上去偷刀 游戏价值 大于20都不推荐，不考虑成就这游戏有没有5小时都不好说

Sometimes you find an imperfect gem; uneven, unclean. I believe Lost in Random is a game what we can call "a diamond in the rough". Positives: +Fluidity of the combat is amazing. +Perfect fit for Deck as it is greatly optimized. +Varied upgrades and card combos keeps the game fresh. +Meaningful and satisfying meta progression. Negatives -Too easy. I'm mediocre at these games and I was able to beat final boss under 5 hours. Of course there is true ending etc but still really easy to break the game. -Weapon variety is too little. While special powers are a nice touch, would be great to have a few more different play styles. -Locations are too samey and most of the time looks uninspired. Lost in Random is fun, fluid and quickly puts you in the action. If you like roguelites there is a high chance you will enjoy this one too. It has enough unique ideas to stand out. However I will only recommend buying it on a deep sale as there isn't enough content for it to be worth for full price. Buy it at least 50% off and you have a solid 8/10 game.

i don't post reviews often, if at all really, but i feel like its warranted in this case. This game is OBJECTIVELY good. i wont deny that it is a fun game to loose some hours to if you like rogue like games similar to Hades. but this is not a good game. ' I bought this game because i played the first one, because i LOVED the first one. Lost in Random was such an amazing game with a, yes admittedly simple, story about two sisters but that's what made it amazing. it HAD a story. it HAD heart to it, SOUL to it. the characters weren't just slapped in with reckless abandon. Spoilers for Lost in Random below! the game Lost in Random takes place in a beautiful world of dice rolls and sisterly bonds. it weaves you into the story. i ADORED the narrator in the the game so much and there's this absolutely amazing part where YOUR narrator gets kidnapped by the queen, and your character even comments on the odd feeling of being suddenly alone. it was such an immersive way to break the fourth wall that it still sits with me today, how many games can you say you've played where your narrator is replaced by the very villain your fighting against? and then you have to break him out of prison? the world in the game is darkly beautiful and constantly had me exploring all i could just to take in every detail. it felt alive. the fighting in the game was amazing as well, the blend of board game/dice rolls/card management was engaging and fun, i constantly had to make sure my deck was best suited for how i liked to play. it was amazing. When i realized they were expanding the story with this game i was excited, i thought we would get more of the queens story, more of the world of random but i was so disappointed. going from a game with so much heart and character to it to...this? a rouge like game with hardly any story, hardly any...anything? it feels hollow. they've stripped away everything that made Lost in Random unique and made it a Hades clone and i don't think ill ever be able to over look that. we need more games that have heart to it. this isn't one of them. if you like rouge like games this is fine but if you want a game with REAL story and character, PLEASE play the original Lost in Random. you wont regret it. TLDR: this game is ok but if you want tim burton meets board games play the original
